blocks.text: Barber Street by home type
Barber Street: streets and boundaries

items.t: Barber Street is a board sub-area name inside the City of Port Moody's Pleasantside neighbourhood, not a City neighbourhood name: the City's Official Community Plan (OCP) Bylaw, 2026, No. 3522, groups Heritage Mountain, Twin Creeks, Noons Creek, Mountain Meadows and Heritage Woods in one section.
The name comes from one street: Barber Street runs off Ioco Road on the north shore of the Port Moody Arm, and Pleasantside Elementary School sits on it at 195 Barber Street.

The working street set is the shore strip below Ioco Road — Barber Street, Alderside Road and the lanes off them — with Ioco Road as the only through road and Old Orchard Park at the west end of the shoreline.

blocks.text: Barber Street: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is primarily single-detached houses, with a small number of townhouse developments along Ioco Road — the OCP's description of the Pleasantside and April Road area this page sits in.

The OCP keeps the expectation low-rise: the lower-density character of Pleasantside and April Road is anticipated to be retained, with gentle densification from Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) over time rather than redevelopment of the shore strip.

blocks.text: Barber Street: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Pleasantside is one of only three Port Moody neighbourhoods where small-lot subdivision is allowed: an eligible Single Detached Residential (RS1) lot can be rezoned to Single Detached Residential – Small Lot (RS1-S), with a minimum lot width of 9 metres and minimum lot area of 325 square metres, in the Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside neighbourhoods only.

The same page sets the clock: small-lot subdivision approval typically takes between twelve and twenty-four months, and a minor development permit and building permit are still required before building on a new RS1-S lot.

blocks.text: Barber Street: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Old Orchard Park connects to the larger Old Mill Site Park/Shoreline Park, together 12.2 hectares, and both are starting points for the Shoreline Trail toward Rocky Point Park.

The community association here is Pleasantside's: the City lists the Pleasantside Community Association, which runs the Penguin Plunge and Boat Festival, and The Residents of Pleasantside IOCO Communities Association (TROPICA) for this shore.

Heritage stock clusters on Ioco Road, not Barber Street itself: the Pleasantside and April Road area carries five properties on the Port Moody Heritage Register in the earlier OCP account, including the Pleasantside Grocery at 631 Ioco Road — check current register status with the City before relying on it.

blocks.text: Barber Street: getting around

items.t: Ioco Road is the only through route: it is designated part of the regional Major Road Network and is the corridor TransLink route 182 uses between Moody Centre Station and the Anmore/Belcarra shore.
The Shoreline Trail is the off-road link: Old Orchard Park is a starting point for walking or cycling the trail toward Rocky Point Park and the Moody Centre station area.

blocks.text: Barber Street: risks and due diligence

items.t: Shoreline lots need the foreshore check: the OCP's environmentally sensitive area and watercourse layers apply along the Port Moody Arm shore, and a lot's status is checked parcel by parcel on the City ViewPort map under Planning and Zoning layers, not on the general pages.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Barber Street?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 11 houses listed in Barber Street. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Barber Street from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses and 0 condos and townhomes sold in Barber Street over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in September with 2 sold.

faq.q: How big is Barber Street compared with the rest of Port Moody?
faq.a: In October 2026, Barber Street held 8.0% of the 138 detached houses listed in Port Moody.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Barber Street than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses rose from 9 in June to 11 in October 2026 (+22.2%).

faq.q: Which school is actually on Barber Street?
faq.a: Pleasantside Elementary School, at 195 Barber Street, a School District No. 43 (SD43) school with office hours 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

faq.q: Can I split a large Ioco Road lot into small lots?
faq.a: The lot must be designated Single Family-Low Density in the OCP and meet the 9-metre width and 325-square-metre area minimums, the City's process runs twelve to twenty-four months in most cases, and planning staff ask applicants to consult before submitting.

faq.q: Why is traffic the first question on this shore?
faq.a: Because the OCP says so directly. Ioco Road is the primary traffic corridor through Pleasantside and April Road and part of the regional Major Road Network, carrying traffic to and from Anmore and Belcarra, and the City records traffic on Ioco Road as a continuing challenge in this neighbourhood.

faq.q: Is there a beach in the neighbourhood?
faq.a: Yes — Old Orchard Park, just under two hectares at the west end of this shore, has Port Moody's only swimming beach (salt-water), and its beach area is used for launching non-motorized boats such as kayaks and stand-up paddleboards, depending on tides.

faq.q: What did houses in Barber Street sell for?
faq.a: 7 houses sold in Barber Street between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,848,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Barber Street?
faq.a: The median was 38 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.3% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
